findings.title: Spawned workers do not pass the multiprocessing.Process type check
findings.body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, whose SpawnProcess class is not a subclass of the top-level multiprocessing.Process class; both inherit from BaseProcess. Consequently this check is false for production workers and a hung worker is never killed before its replacement starts. If the original worker resumes, both workers can flush the same shards and update the same health/backpressure state, potentially producing duplicate segments. The identical check in join() also skips termination. Use BaseProcess or the actual spawn-context process class to distinguish processes from test threads.

findings.title: Terminate remaining workers when the join deadline expires
findings.body: Once the join deadline expires, this break skips cleanup of every remaining worker. This happens if next_step.join() consumes the timeout or an earlier flusher takes the remaining time. Setting stopped only requests cooperative shutdown: workers blocked in Redis or Kafka calls can remain alive after join returns and retain ownership of shards that are reassigned during a rebalance. Even after correcting the process type checks, all remaining processes need termination when the shared deadline is exhausted, rather than exiting the cleanup loop.
